claims: Runs entirely on your own machine: no API keys, no monthly subscriptions, no usage limits
Clones voices from a few seconds of audio
System-wide dictation hotkey that types into any app
Setup takes less than a minute: paste one command into terminal
how_to_steps: Paste the one-line install command into the terminal
Open Voicebox, record a few seconds of audio to clone a voice
Use the push-to-talk / hold-key dictation to type into any app
on_screen_only: README tabs: README, Contributing, MIT license, Security; badges: downloads 1.5M, release v0.5.0, stars 33k, license MIT, 'Ask DeepWiki'
'Clone voice' dialog with waveform, Name / Description / Reference Text / Language fields and 'Create Profile' button
'PUSH TO TALK -- hold the key and just |' dictation overlay
Creator wears 'AIS' branded shirt; DM word 'VOICEBOX'
cta: DM 'VOICEBOX' on Instagram for the link; link in bio

relevance.why: Local dictation could save a time-poor founder typing time in Claude Code, but voice cloning is not core to building apps; quality of local models vs Wispr Flow is unverified.

implement_score.why: Low effort to try if the repo is real and runs on a Mac, but local TTS/STT needs GPU/CPU headroom and probably a Python/ML stack; marginal over built-in macOS dictation unless accuracy is high.

verify: Exact GitHub owner/repo for 'voicebox' (not shown) and whether it really has 33k stars / 1.5M downloads
